title: qa/issues.jsonl carries 4 ids that are not plain ISS-<digits>, so the allocator (and any strict form check) refuses the real ledger
evidence: node scripts/qa/ledger-alloc-cli.mjs verify on the real union (475 rows) reports 4 wrong-form findings and exits 1: issues.jsonl:142 ISS-C-CLAIMS-TARGETING-001, :143 ISS-C-TOPICREFS-ARG-001 (lane-form ids from the c-* lane merged into the canonical file), :358 ISS-360-OBSFLAKE, :359 ISS-360-HEARTBEAT (qualified repair ids from the ISS-360 duplicate incident). No duplicate ids and no unparseable lines exist. Because the allocator fails closed, `append` and `next-id` cannot be used on the real ledger until this is resolved.
fix_direction: Approver decision, NOT a row edit by the maker (C4/D-019: ids are never renumbered): either grandfather exactly these four ids in a named allowlist the allocator reads, or accept `ISS-<QUALIFIER>-<digits|WORD>` as legal in the main file. Do not rename the rows.
verified_evidence: cycle 1 re-check (qa/verdicts/iss-298-ledger-id-allocator.md, commit d1fb6d0): `node scripts/qa/ledger-alloc-cli.mjs verify` on the real union prints rows=479 findings=0, exit 0; my own script confirms all 479 ids match the reading grammar and the four ids (ISS-C-CLAIMS-TARGETING-001, ISS-C-TOPICREFS-ARG-001, ISS-360-OBSFLAKE, ISS-360-HEARTBEAT) are accepted. Cause was the tool's over-strict reader; no Approver decision was needed (D-019/D-055 already make those ids lawful) and no row was edited.

title: 6 main-ledger rows (ISS-117, 314, 362, 363, 366, 372) have no `feature` field, so no citation check can attribute them
evidence: Found while running cite-check over the real tree; rows at issues.jsonl lines 117, 312, 361, 362, 365, 371. The allocator's append requires `feature`, so new rows cannot repeat this.
fix_direction: File-don't-fix per D-014 low class; any backfill is a lifecycle edit needing its own authorization (I1).

title: C3 citation check has no unit-to-feature mapping, so on the real tree it can only report CANDIDATES (94 of 266 ISSUES-WRITTEN citations, 146 unattributed)
evidence: cite-check on the real tree: units=472 cited=266 unattributed=146 mismatches=94 (belongs-to-other-unit; 0 unresolved). Naive row.feature != unit slug flags 240 of 266, almost all legitimate (units file under broader feature slugs). The 94 include legitimate cases where the feature slug coincides with a unit name (e.g. golden-set-recall), so they are not asserted defects.
fix_direction: Needs a decision on how a unit declares its feature (manifest `Feature:` is free prose today). Until then cite-check is a triage tool, not a gate.

title: acquireLock busy-spins forever (no sleep, no 8 s deadline) when the lock file cannot be created because of EACCES/EPERM/EBUSY and does not exist
evidence: In scripts/qa/ledger-alloc.mjs acquireLock, EACCES/EPERM/EBUSY/EEXIST are all 'contention'; the follow-up statSync then throws ENOENT (no lock file exists) and the catch does `continue`, which skips both the waitMs deadline check and the sleep. Reproduction (temp copy only): mkdir T/qa, copy a one-row issues.jsonl in, `icacls T/qa /deny product:(WD,AD)`, then `node scripts/qa/ledger-alloc-cli.mjs append --main --row row.json --root T` -> still running after 20 s at 100% of a core until killed (expected: exit 1 within ~8 s with a clear message). It fails closed (nothing is written) but hangs, and the documented 8 s timeout does not hold; on this machine a spinning process steals CPU from the production worker.
fix_direction: Count the deadline and sleep on the ENOENT-after-contention path too, and surface a persistent EACCES/EPERM as a hard error naming the directory after a few retries. Add a test that makes the directory unwritable (or stubs openSync) and asserts a non-zero exit inside the wait bound.
verified_evidence: cycle 1 re-check (qa/verdicts/iss-298-ledger-id-allocator.md, commit d1fb6d0): icacls-denied qa dir, append --main exits 1 in under 2 s with `cannot create ledger lock ...: EPERM ... This is not contention`, no lock left, no spin; fresh lock in a denied dir times out at the 8 s overall deadline; stale lock reported, not stolen. Mutation 'remove overall deadline' and 'treat every lock error as contention' are both killed. A separate transient-EPERM race under contention is filed as ISS-ALLOC-005.

title: acquireLock reports a spurious 'cannot create ledger lock ... EPERM ... This is not contention' when another process's lock is mid-delete on Windows and the file has vanished by the time it is stat'ed
evidence: scripts/qa/ledger-alloc.mjs acquireLock: openSync(wx) throws EPERM while the holder's unlinkSync is pending; the code then statSync()s the lock, gets ENOENT (already gone), and because code !== 'EEXIST' falls to lockFail(), which says the failure is not contention. Reproduction on a temp copy of the real ledger files (no real ledger touched), harness = N node child processes each calling appendRow 20 times, default 8 s wait: 13 processes (4 main, 4 lane a, 4 lane b, 1 alloc) x 3 runs gave other-errors 1, 1, 3 (all 'cannot create ledger lock ...: EPERM'); 4 processes x 20 x 4 runs gave 1 such failure in 4 runs. In every run: dupIds=0, unparseable=0, rows added == successful appends, no lock left. So it fails closed and a retry succeeds, but the diagnosis is wrong and a caller that trusts 'fix the directory permissions' would chase a non-problem. (Also noted: at 13-way contention on the ~1 MB real ledger 4 to 18 of 260 appends hit the 8 s deadline; at 4-way, 0 to 1 of 80.)
fix_direction: In the stat-ENOENT catch, treat EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY like EEXIST (retry within the deadline) when the open error was one of those: a vanished lock file means the holder just released it. Only a persistent error across the whole deadline, or one with no lock file ever seen, should be reported as a permission problem. Add a test that stubs openSync to throw EPERM once then succeed.
